chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm who said:
Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Muhammad, what do you say about a man who marries a Christian woman in preference to a Muslim woman?'

I said: 'I am your ransom, and what is my opinion before your opinion?' He said: 'You will say it, for you know my opinion by my statement.' I said: 'The marriage of a Christian woman to a Muslim man is not permissible, nor is the marriage of a non-Muslim woman [to a Muslim man].'
He said: 'Why?' I said: 'Because of the statement of Allah, the Exalted: 'And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe.''
'And [also] chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you.'
I said: 'His statement: 'And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe' abrogates this verse.' He smiled and then remained silent.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a Muslim man marrying a Christian woman according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this dialogue from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) engages al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm on the specific juristic issue of prioritizing a Christian wife over a Muslim one. The narrator argues that the general prohibition in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:221) abrogates the specific permission in Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:5) regarding the People of the Book, a view the Imam confirms through his characteristic silence (sukut). This highlights the Shia scholarly consensus that while marriage to chaste People of the Book is permissible, it is not preferred over a Muslim woman, and some scholars view the permission as abrogated by the later, more comprehensive verse.
